claims.text: Rapid quenching of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 at approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s produces only partial amorphization and a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
Standard rapid-quenching and reheating protocols produce primary non-eutectic crystalline phases alongside an amorphous phase in this alloy.
An isothermal hold immediately after rapid quenching can enhance amorphous retention and thermal stability.
The proposed hold temperature is approximately 850 K, identified as 0.8–0.85 of the crystallization-onset temperature.
The proposed isothermal-hold duration is 20–30 seconds.
The isothermal hold promotes atomic-scale relaxation.
Atomic-scale relaxation reduces free volume or free-volume agglomeration.
Reduced free-volume agglomeration stabilizes the disordered amorphous configuration.
During the hold, undercooled atoms rearrange into a relaxed, lower-energy amorphous state.
Formation of a relaxed, lower-energy amorphous state decreases the thermodynamic driving force for crystalline-phase nucleation during reheating.
The resulting reduction in nucleation suppresses primary crystallization during subsequent reheating.
Held samples will retain a higher amorphous fraction than otherwise identically processed samples without the hold.
Held samples will exhibit a delayed crystallization-onset temperature during reheating relative to controls without the hold.
The beneficial effect is confined to a narrow window near 850 K and 20–30 seconds.
Departures from the proposed hold window may cause either premature crystallization or inadequate atomic relaxation.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that reheating should not exceed the delayed crystallization onset, whereas measuring crystallization exothermic-peak characteristics by DSC ordinarily requires reheating into and through the crystallization event.
